items.t: PowerShift automatic shudders and jerks from a stop
items.job: Replace dual clutch assembly and input shaft seals, then relearn
items.note: CarComplaints owners report about $500 for shudder repairs and around $1,600 for clutch work. Ask a dealer whether any extended clutch coverage applies to your VIN.

items.t: Transmission control module failure
items.job: Replace and program transmission control module
items.note: Ford extended coverage on this module to 10 years or 150,000 miles on many cars, so check your VIN before paying.

items.t: Automatic transmission fails and needs replacing
items.job: Replace PowerShift transmission with a new or remanufactured unit
items.note: CarComplaints owners report average bills of about $3,400 (2011) to $4,800 (2014).

items.t: Transmission seal leak soaks the clutches
items.job: Replace transmission input shaft seals and contaminated clutch
items.note: If the clutch is still clean, sealing the leak alone costs much less.

items.t: Doors won't latch or may open while driving (recall)
items.job: Replace side door latches
items.note: Free at a Ford dealer under the door latch recalls.

items.t: Fuel pump can fail and stall the engine (recall)
items.job: Replace fuel pump

items.t: Fuel tank may leak (recall)
items.job: Replace fuel tank

items.t: Right side curtain airbag may not deploy (recall)
items.job: Reprogram airbag control module

items.t: Cylinder head can crack if coolant runs low (recall)
items.job: Install coolant level sensor and update engine software
items.note: The recall adds a warning; a head that has already cracked from overheating is a separate, much bigger repair.

items.t: Coolant loss and head gasket failure (ST)
items.job: Replace head gasket and resurface cylinder head
items.note: Finding and fixing a small external leak early costs a few hundred dollars instead.

items.t: Coolant leak from thermostat housing or water pump
items.job: Replace thermostat housing or water pump and refill coolant
items.note: The thermostat housing is the cheaper job; the water pump takes longer.

items.t: Coolant loss and white smoke (1.0L EcoBoost)
items.job: Replace cylinder head with integrated exhaust manifold
items.note: Diagnosis with an extended pressure test comes first; costs drop a lot if an external leak is found.

items.t: Turbo wastegate rattle (1.0L EcoBoost)
items.job: Repair or replace turbo wastegate linkage
items.note: If the linkage cannot be serviced on its own, the turbo may need replacing, which costs far more.

items.t: Lack of power and misfire codes (1.0L EcoBoost)
items.job: Diagnose misfire, replace ignition coil or spark plugs

items.t: Low boost and lack of power (ST)
items.job: Replace boost control solenoid and check boost hoses

items.t: Turbo wastegate rattle on cold start (ST)
items.job: Replace turbo wastegate actuator

items.t: Carbon buildup causes rough idle (ST)
items.job: Walnut-blast clean intake valves

items.t: Manual clutch slipping or hard to select gears (ST)
items.job: Replace clutch kit
items.note: Worn gearbox synchronizers are a separate, more expensive repair.

items.t: Front brakes may drag and overheat (recall)
items.job: Flush brake fluid, replace front calipers and hoses

items.t: Backup camera shows blank or distorted image (recall)
items.job: Inspect and replace rearview camera

items.t: Blower fan only works on high
items.job: Replace blower motor resistor

items.t: No heat on cold mornings from frozen blower motor
items.job: Replace blower motor and fuse, seal water entry at the cowl

items.t: Rough running or no start from ignition coil fault
items.job: Replace ignition coil

items.t: Hard start after refueling
items.job: Replace canister purge valve

items.t: Radio or SYNC freezes or stops working
items.job: Update SYNC software or replace audio module
items.note: A software update or battery reset costs little; a replacement module is the high end.

items.t: Clunking over bumps from worn shocks or struts
items.job: Replace front struts or rear shocks (pair)
